question: Newton's first law of motion is also known as ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Law of Inertia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Law of Inertia, **Newton's first law of motion, states that an object at rest tends to stay at rest, and an object in motion tends to stay in motion unless acted upon by an external force.**
 
• The term **'inertia' refers to the resistance of an object to change its state of motion.**
 
• It can be thought of as a property of mass to resist change.
 
• If an object is at rest,** it will remain at rest unless an unbalanced force acts upon it.**
 
• If an object is in motion**, it will continue to move in a straight line at a constant speed unless acted upon by an unbalanced force.**
 
• This law introduces the concept of a frame of reference.
 
• The descriptions of motion** depend on the observer, and different observers may observe different states of motion.**
 
• An important consequence of this law is the** idea of conservation of momentum.**
 
• If the net force on an object is zero,** its momentum (mass times velocity) remains constant.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Newton's Laws of Motion include three fundamental principles:**
 
• **Newton's First Law (Law of Inertia):**
 
 
• **​**An object will remain at** rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force.**
 
 
 
• **Newton's Second Law:**
 
 
• **​**The rate of change of momentum of an object is directly proportional to the force applied.
 
• It is typically formulated as ***F=ma*, where F is the force applied, m is the mass of the object, and a is the acceleration produced.**
 
 
 
• **Newton's Third Law:**
 
 
• **​**For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
 
• It means that any force exerted on a **body will create a force of equal magnitude but in the opposite direction on the object which exerted the first force.**
